title: Brief special meeting leads to closed session
subtitle: Council authorized a private session on negotiations and a solicitor-client privilege matter; no public decisions followed.
overview: Kitchener City Council held a short special meeting on February 6, 2026, chaired by the Mayor. The meeting opened with a Land Acknowledgement. No one declared a pecuniary interest, and the Mayor had no business or updates to report.

The only substantive action was a motion to hold a closed (in-camera) meeting right after the special meeting. Council approved it {{vote:m1}}. The closed session was to consider a position or procedure to be applied to negotiations, and a matter covered by solicitor-client privilege. These are permitted closed-meeting topics under the Municipal Act.

The meeting adjourned at about 3:30 p.m. The minutes record no public decisions on the closed-session topics. Residents should know that the subject matter stays private for now, and any outcome would need to be reported publicly at a later date. The minutes give no further detail.

decisions.detail: Council agreed to hold an in-camera meeting after the special meeting to consider a position or procedure for negotiations and a solicitor-client privilege matter {{vote:m1}}.
